name: proof
description: Use Proof for verifiable identity, x401 credential presentation, e-signing, and remote online notarization.

interface.longDescription: Proof brings digital trust workflows into ChatGPT. Users can present Verifiable Credentials through x401, upload documents and begin e-signing or remote online notarization, and use supported identity and account capabilities exposed by Proof. A Proof account and OAuth authorization are required. Credential presentation and signing actions remain subject to user approval in Proof.
defaultPrompt: Use my Proof identity to satisfy this x401 credential request.
Help me e-sign a PDF with Proof.
Start an online notarization for my document with Proof.

positive.description: Prepare one attached PDF for a Proof e-sign workflow.
positive.prompt: Help me e-sign the attached PDF with Proof.
positive.expected_behavior: Requests a one-time upload URL for the attached PDF, uploads it, then calls start_esign with the returned file_id and gives the user the returned activation URL without claiming the document is already signed.

positive.description: Prepare one attached PDF for remote online notarization.
positive.prompt: I need this attached document notarized online through Proof.
positive.expected_behavior: Requests a one-time upload URL for the PDF, uploads it, then calls start_notarization with the returned file_id and gives the user the activation URL for identity verification and the notary meeting.

positive.description: Exercise the documented three-document boundary for e-signing.
positive.prompt: Start a Proof e-sign transaction for these three attached PDFs in the order I attached them.
positive.tools_triggered: request_document_upload_url for each PDF, then start_esign
positive.expected_behavior: Obtains and uses a distinct file_id for each of the three PDFs, preserves attachment order in the documents array, and returns the activation URL and transaction identifier.

positive.description: Exercise the documented three-document boundary for notarization.
positive.prompt: Start one Proof online notarization for these three attached PDFs.
positive.tools_triggered: request_document_upload_url for each PDF, then start_notarization
positive.expected_behavior: Uploads all three PDFs, calls start_notarization once with exactly three file_id values, and returns the activation URL and transaction identifier without claiming notarization is complete.

positive.description: Complete an x401 Verifiable Credential presentation after a protected site returns a PROOF-REQUEST header.
positive.prompt: Use my Proof identity to satisfy the credential request from this x401-protected site.
positive.expected_behavior: Passes the protected origin and unchanged PROOF-REQUEST value to x401_start_presentation, shows the returned approval link when approval is required, polls x401_get_presentation only as directed, and sends the single-use PROOF-RESPONSE only to the returned site when ready.

negative.description: Do not accept unsupported non-PDF input for document workflows.
negative.prompt: Use Proof to notarize this attached JPEG image.
negative.expected_behavior: Explains that the available Proof upload workflow requires a PDF and does not call request_document_upload_url, start_notarization, or start_esign for the JPEG.

negative.description: Do not exceed the documented three-document transaction limit.
negative.prompt: Start one Proof e-sign transaction for these four attached PDFs.
negative.expected_behavior: Explains that one transaction supports up to three uploaded PDFs and asks the user to reduce or split the set; it does not call start_esign with four documents.

negative.description: Do not use Proof tools for unrelated identity-free work.
negative.prompt: Summarize this public news article for me.
negative.expected_behavior: Handles the request without invoking any Proof MCP tool because no credential, signature, notarization, or Proof account capability is needed.

publication.release_notes: Initial public release with x401 Verifiable Credential presentation, PDF e-signing, and remote online notarization workflows.
